About us

About Friends Law Chamber

Friends Law Chamber is led by Ch Waqas Riaz Gujjar, Advocate High Court, and works from the District Courts, Sargodha. We handle family, criminal, property, civil and banking cases, and act for overseas Pakistanis who cannot be in Pakistan.

Clients come to us for straight advice, including when the outlook is difficult. We explain every step, agree the fee first and keep you updated after every hearing.

Legal guides

Plain-language guides to the questions we hear most often. These are general information, not legal advice.

Questions and answers

Short answers to what people ask us first.

What should I bring to the first meeting?

Your CNIC, and any papers about the case: FIR copy, court notices, agreements, property documents or cheques. If you have nothing yet, come anyway and we will tell you what to collect.

How much does a consultation cost?

The fee is agreed before the meeting starts. Call or message the office and we will tell you the consultation fee and the likely cost of taking your case forward.

Can you tell me how long my case will take?

Every case is different, and courts set their own dates. We will give you an honest estimate based on similar cases, but nobody can promise a result or an exact date.

Is what I tell you kept private?

Yes. Everything you share with your advocate is confidential.

I live abroad. Can I hire you without coming to Pakistan?

In many matters, yes. The first consultation can be by phone or WhatsApp call, and documents can be sent as photos or PDF. For some court cases a power of attorney is needed, and we will tell you exactly what is required for your matter.

What is the difference between bail before and after arrest?

Bail before arrest is asked for when you fear you will be arrested. Bail after arrest is asked for once you are already in custody. Which one applies, and how strong your case is, depends on the facts, so speak to a lawyer quickly.

How is khula different from talaq?

Talaq is pronounced by the husband and must follow the notice procedure in law. Khula is a divorce the wife asks for through the family court. The steps and the financial consequences differ, so get advice before filing or replying.

What papers do I need for a money recovery case?

Anything that proves the money was given and not returned: a written agreement, receipt, cheque, bank transfer proof, messages, and any notice you have already sent. Bring your CNIC too.
